meta_title: Guard Spec — self-hosted prompt-injection firewall for LLM apps
meta_description: Open-source gateway that stops prompt injection before it reaches your LLM. Checks prompts, documents, tool results and MCP tools, and guards the answer. English and Vietnamese.
hero_title: Stop prompt injection before it reaches your LLM
hero_lead: Guard Spec is a gateway between your apps and any OpenAI-compatible API. It checks prompts, retrieved documents, tool results and MCP tools on the way in, and the model's answer on the way out. Prompts never leave your network.
code_same: the rest of your code stays the same
code_blocked_title: when a request carries an injection
problem_title: Your LLM reads text that you did not write
problem_lead: Chatbots, RAG assistants and agents pass user input, web pages, documents and tool output straight into the model. Any of them can carry instructions that override yours.
threat1_p: A user types “ignore your previous instructions” in a hundred disguises: leetspeak, homoglyphs, Vietnamese teencode, text without diacritics.
threat2_p: A web page, email or PDF in your knowledge base hides an instruction in invisible HTML, Unicode tag characters or bidi tricks.
threat3_p: An MCP server describes a tool with hidden steps that tell your agent to read secrets and send them elsewhere.
how_title: One gateway in front of every LLM call
how_lead: Point your SDK's base URL at Guard Spec. Every request is sanitized, scored by three detection layers and checked against your policies. Clean requests go on; injections get a 400 and an alert.
context_alt: Guard Spec between your AI apps and the LLM providers
l0_p: Strips invisible characters, Unicode tags and bidi overrides; flags anomalies.
l1_p: Fast pattern rules that see through diacritics, teencode, leetspeak and homoglyphs.
l2_p: Our own ONNX model, trained for English and Vietnamese, running in process.
l3_p: Embedding match against known attack exemplars you can add to.
pol_p: Per-organization rules compiled to CEL: allow, block, log or route.
out_p: Catches exfiltration links, personal data and a leaked canary, also when streaming.
feat_title: Everything a security team needs around the detector
f1_p: Rules, a classifier and similarity search are fused into one score with a clear threshold. Run rules only, or all three.
f2_p: Built and evaluated for both, including Vietnamese with and without diacritics, teencode and leetspeak.
f3_p: Runs in your network. No prompt goes to a third-party moderation API. Every rule is readable and editable.
f4_p: Change one base URL. Route to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, vLLM or Ollama per organization and project.
f5_p: Blocked requests reach Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, email, signed SIEM webhooks or a SOC agent over A2A.
f6_p: OpenID Connect single sign-on (Entra ID, Okta, Google, Keycloak), TOTP two-factor, org-wide login rules.
f7_p: Organizations, projects, roles and API keys with rate limits, backed by Postgres row-level security.
f8_p: One row per request (content off by default) and a log of every configuration and security change.
f9_p: Docker Compose, a Helm chart and an air-gapped image. Signed images, SBOMs, Prometheus and OpenTelemetry.
admin_title: See every decision, change every rule
admin_lead: A bilingual admin console for the security team, in light and dark.
admin_1: Dashboard and live request flow through each layer
admin_2: Policy editor, as text or visual, with a simulator
admin_3: Providers, routing, request log and audit
admin_4: Alert rules, channels, members and security settings
admin_alt: Guard Spec admin UI showing the request flow
bench_lead: All three layers with the default classifier, on our eval set of 2,176 rows (1,171 attacks, 1,005 benign; 926 English, 1,250 Vietnamese).
stat_tpr: attacks blocked at the default threshold
bench_note: Measured on 2026-11-04 on an Apple M3 Max; latency is the detector in process, not end-to-end HTTP. The Vietnamese data is synthetic, and benign Vietnamese teencode is still blocked 3.5% of the time. The README lists every number, its limits and the commands to reproduce it.
cmp_r1c: A network service in front of the model: any language can use it, and you change a base URL, not your code
cmp_r2c: Self-hosted: prompts never leave your network, and you can read and change every rule
cmp_r3c: Its own classifier is one of several layers, with sanitization, policies, an output guard and an audit log around it
qs_lead: You need Docker with Compose v2. One script writes strong random secrets, pulls the signed images and the models (SHA-256 verified), and waits until all three layers are ready.
band_title: Put a guard in front of your LLM
band_lead: Free and open source under Apache-2.0. Star the repo, try it on your own traffic, and tell us what it misses.

pg_meta_title: Playground — try Guard Spec in your browser
pg_meta_description: Type a prompt, a RAG document or an MCP tool description and see what Guard Spec decides: the fused score, the L1, L2 and L3 layers, and why. Prompts are not stored.
pg_h1: Try Guard Spec in your browser
pg_lead: Type a prompt, paste a retrieved document or an MCP tool description, and see what the gateway decides: the fused score, each detection layer and the reason. Nothing to install.
pg_placeholder: Type or paste a prompt, or pick a sample below…
pg_notice: Prompts are not stored. The playground keeps no copy of what you type and no IP address, only counters. It never calls an LLM: it runs the detector and nothing else. Up to 4 KB per scan, 10 scans a minute.
pg_empty: Pick a sample or type something, then press Scan.
pg_no_layers: This gateway does not report per-layer scores yet.
pg_why_fusion: strongest layer of the fused score
pg_why_cascade: decisive on its own, L2 and L3 skipped
pg_why_l1_floor: a decisive rule set the floor of the score
pg_why_mcp_signals: known poisoning patterns in the description
pg_san_clean: No hidden or invisible characters found.
pg_san_tool: MCP tool descriptions are sanitized inside the tool scan; signals are listed below.
pg_f_removed_chars: {n} bytes of invisible characters removed before scoring
pg_err_too_long: The text is longer than {max} bytes. Shorten it and try again.
pg_err_rate: Too many scans from your address. Try again in {s} seconds.
pg_err_busy: The playground is busy. Try again in a few seconds.
pg_err_challenge: The anti-abuse check failed. Reload the page and try again.
pg_err_generic: The scan failed. Try again later.
pg_err_network: Could not reach the playground. Check your connection and try again.
pg_more: The playground calls POST /guardrail/scan on a Guard Spec gateway with all three layers. Run the same gateway in your own network in five minutes and put it in front of your LLM.
